cor-ub-additive.title: Main effects in the additive model
cor-ub-additive.title_html: Main effects in the additive model
cor-ub-additive.html:
In the two-way layout with all cells occupied, let R=Ca⊤⊗Cb⊤. Then:

  1. 𝛍μ^R is the table of fitted cell means of the additive model, and SSER−SSE=SS(AB∣μ,A,B);

  2. for any weights w∈Rb with ∑jwj≠0, the hypothesis that ∑jwjμij is the same for all i is, within the additive model, the hypothesis α1=⋯=αa. Its sum of squares is SS(A∣μ,B), whatever w;

  3. weights that differ from row to row do not have this property: the hypothesis that ∑jwijμij is the same for all i depends on the column effects unless ∑jwijβj does not depend on i.

def-ub-cell-means.title: Cell-means model
def-ub-cell-means.html: Let factors F1,…,Fk have a1,…,ak levels. A cell is a combination ω=(i1,…,ik) of levels, and there are p=a1a2⋯ak cells. Cell ω contains nω≥0 observations yω1,…,yωnω. It is occupied if nω≥1 and empty otherwise. Write O for the set of occupied cells, m=|O| and n=∑ωnω. The cell-means model is yωl=μω+εωl,l=1,…,nω, with errors that are uncorrelated with mean zero and variance σ2, and independent N(0,σ2) when we test. In matrix form 𝛍E(Y)=Wμ, where 𝛍μ∈Rp collects the cell means and W is the n×p matrix whose column ω indicates the observations in cell ω. We write D=W⊤W=diag(nω), and y¯ω for the average of an occupied cell.

eq-ub-cell-f.html: F=(Ly¯−d)⊤(LD+L⊤)−1(Ly¯−d)qs2∼F(q,n−m,γH),

eq-ub-coding-hypothesis.html: ∑jwjμij  is the same for all i.

eq-ub-constrained-estimate.html: 𝛍𝛍μ^R=VRDy¯,VR=K(K⊤DK)−1K⊤,Cov(μ^R)=σ2VR,

eq-ub-constrained-f.html: 𝛍𝛍F=(Lμ^R)⊤(LVRL⊤)−Lμ^RqsR2,sR2=SSERn−p+g,

eq-ub-kronecker-hypotheses.html: 𝛍𝛍𝛍HA: (Ca⊤⊗b−11b⊤)μ=0,HB: (a−11a⊤⊗Cb⊤)μ=0,HAB: (Ca⊤⊗Cb⊤)μ=0.

eq-ub-type2-a.html: ∑jnij(μij−μ¯⋅jw)=0for i=1,…,a;

eq-ub-type2-b.html: ∑inij(μij−μ¯iw)=0for j=1,…,b;

exm-ub-additive-trial.title: The variety trial under additivity
exm-ub-additive-trial.html:
In @exm-ub-types-trial the interaction sum of squares 2.146 gave F=1.71 on 4 and 28 degrees of freedom, p=0.176. Suppose we accept additivity. The constrained fit @eq-ub-constrained-estimate gives the table of fitted means

S1 S2 S3
V1 5.56 7.17 7.95
V2 5.11 6.73 7.51
V3 4.48 6.09 6.87

with SSER=10.927 on 37−9+4=32 degrees of freedom and sR2=0.3415. The fitted mean of V1 at S3 is 7.95, although its two plots averaged 7.45: additivity carries V1’s advantage at S1 and S2 over to S3. The test of equal unweighted variety means, @eq-ub-constrained-f, gives 6.184, the Type II sum of squares, with F=9.06 on 2 and 32 degrees of freedom, p=0.00076. The script checks that site weights 0.5,0.3,0.2, and the column S1 alone, give the same 6.184 (@cor-ub-additive(b)), while each variety’s own count weights give 0.571, the Type I value. The least squares means are 6.894, 6.449 and 5.811 (standard errors 0.169, 0.170, 0.178), and V1 exceeds V2 by 0.445 (standard error 0.243).

The generating means had a small interaction: V1’s advantage over V2 is 0.8 at S1, 0.7 at S2 and 0.1 at S3, and the test on 4 and 28 degrees of freedom has little power to detect it. A non-significant interaction test is not evidence of additivity.

exm-ub-empty-trial.title: The variety trial with two empty cells
exm-ub-empty-trial.title_html: The variety trial with two empty cells
exm-ub-empty-trial.html:
Suppose that in the trial of @exm-ub-variety-trial V1 had never been grown at S3, nor V3 at S1. That leaves n=33 plots in m=7 cells, with 26 error degrees of freedom and error mean square 0.3096. The design graph (Figure 17.4.1) is connected, so the estimable interaction contrasts have dimension 7−3−3+1=2, spanned by two tetrads. The interaction sum of squares is 1.218, F=1.97, p=0.160, and the script checks that the tetrads give the same value through @eq-ub-cell-f. The six-cell contrast around V1–S1–V2–S3–V3–S2–V1 is the difference of the tetrads (@exr-ub-hexad).

The unweighted means of V1 and V3 are no longer estimable. V1 and V2 share S1 and S2, and the difference of their averages there is 0.603 (standard error 0.268). The additive model is still identified. Its Type II sum of squares for varieties is 5.766 on 2 degrees of freedom, and it fills the empty cells with 8.32 for V1 at S3 and 4.20 for V3 at S1. The first exceeds every observed cell mean: V1’s advantage at S1 and S2 is carried to a site where V1 was never grown, although in the generating means it had nearly vanished there (the true mean is 7.6).

The “Type III” sum of squares for varieties is 0 on 0 degrees of freedom: V2 is the only complete row (@thm-ub-empty-cells(d)). If only V1 at S3 is removed, it is 2.027 on 1 degree of freedom, the sum of squares of μ¯2⋅=μ¯3⋅, for every ordering of the levels.

exm-ub-threeway.title: Simplifying a three-factor curing study
exm-ub-threeway.html:
A (synthetic) study of a resin coating measured hardness after curing at three temperatures (T), with two hardeners (H) and resin from three suppliers (S). The 18 cells received one to three panels each, 37 in all, so the full model [THS] leaves 19 error degrees of freedom, with mean square 0.408. The backward path:

Step From To Term removed df SS F p
1 [THS] [TH][TS][HS] THS 4 1.137 0.70 0.6036
2 [TH][TS][HS] [TH][HS] TS 4 1.845 1.13 0.3719
3 [TH][HS] [TH][S] HS 2 4.132 5.06 0.0173
4 [TH][HS] [T][HS] TH 2 13.716 16.81 0.0001
5 [TH][HS] [HS] T and TH 4 19.100 11.70 0.0001

Steps 1 and 2 cost little. Step 1 is the test of the constraints 𝛍G3μ=0 with G3=C3⊤⊗C2⊤⊗C3⊤, and the script recovers its sum of squares from the cell means through @thm-ub-constrained(b). Steps 3 and 4 show that neither interaction with the hardener can go, so the path stops at [TH][HS]. In that model the effect of temperature under a given hardener is the same for all three suppliers, so whether temperature matters at all is a single question inside the model, answered by step 5.

exm-ub-types-trial.title: Five tables for one data set
exm-ub-types-trial.title_html: Five tables for one data set
exm-ub-types-trial.html:
The table has the layout of @exm-ss-anes-types in Chapter 9, and the listing computes its entries the same way, as squared lengths of projections. For the trial of @exm-ub-variety-trial:

Term df Type I, variety first Type I, site first Type II Type III reference coding
variety 2 0.571 6.184 6.184 4.958 3.601
site 2 31.175 25.562 31.175 27.634 7.456
interaction 4 2.146 2.146 2.146 2.146 2.146
residual 28 8.781 8.781 8.781 8.781 8.781

Only the Type I columns add up to the model sum of squares 33.892; the Type II and Type III entries add up to 39.506 and 34.738. The verdicts on varieties differ. Entered first, F=0.91 and p=0.414: the raw averages 6.423, 6.583 and 6.275 mix each variety with the sites it was grown at. After sites (Type II), F=9.86 and p=0.001. Type III gives F=7.90 and p=0.002, the test of @exm-ub-variety-trial. The last column compares the varieties at S1 only (F=5.74, p=0.008).

The script checks every entry against statsmodels’ anova_lm (types 1, 2 and 3, with sum-to-zero and Helmert coding for type 3), and recovers each entry from the matrix L of its part of @thm-ub-types. It also confirms @prp-ub-coding: reference coding of the varieties with contrast coding of the sites reproduces 4.958, and a random coding of the sites gives the sum of squares of @eq-ub-coding-hypothesis.

exm-ub-variety-trial.title: Three varieties at three sites
exm-ub-variety-trial.html:
A (synthetic) trial compared three wheat varieties V1, V2 and V3 at three sites S1, S2 and S3, with yield in tonnes per hectare. Each site grew mostly the variety it already knew. There are 37 plots in the m=9 cells:

S1 S2 S3 all sites
V1 7 plots, 5.73 4, 7.12 2, 7.45 13, 6.423
V2 3, 4.67 5, 6.98 4, 7.53 12, 6.583
V3 2, 4.55 3, 5.73 7, 7.00 12, 6.275

The last column gives each variety’s raw average, the estimate of its weighted mean μ¯iw. The pooled within-cell variance is s2=0.3136 on n−m=28 degrees of freedom, so the standard errors of the cell averages range from 0.212 (seven plots) to 0.396 (two plots).

Figure 17.1.1 shows the table. V1 is the best variety at S1 and S2 and nearly ties with V2 at S3, yet its raw average, 6.423, is below that of V2, 6.583, because V1 was grown mostly at the poorest site. The unweighted means 6.768, 6.391 and 5.761 compare the varieties over the same three sites, and V1 comes first. Their standard errors, 0.176, 0.165 and 0.184, exceed those of the raw averages (0.155, 0.162 and 0.162), as @prp-ub-marginal-means requires. For V1 the ratio depends only on the counts: 13(1/7+1/4+1/2)/3=11.607/3≈1.136.

The tests @eq-ub-kronecker-hypotheses, computed with @eq-ub-cell-f, give F=7.90 on 2 and 28 degrees of freedom for equal unweighted variety means (p=0.0019), F=44.06 for equal unweighted site means, and F=1.71 on 4 and 28 degrees of freedom for additivity (p=0.1755). The difference between V1 and V2, averaged over sites without weights, is estimated as 0.377 with standard error 0.242. With t28,0.025=2.048, the 95% interval is from −0.12 to 0.87. The raw averages give a difference of −0.160, with the opposite sign.

exr-ub-2x2-empty.title: B1
exr-ub-2x2-empty.html: In a 2×2 layout with cell (2,2) empty, show that the additive model estimates μ22 by y¯21+y¯12−y¯11, and find its variance. Show that the last-in sum of squares of A with sum-to-zero coding is identically zero. Compare with @exr-ss-empty-cell.

exr-ub-additive-2x2.title: B1
exr-ub-additive-2x2.html: For a 2×2 layout with all cells occupied, take R=(1,−1,−1,1). Use @thm-ub-constrained(b) to show that the additive fit is μ^ij=y¯ij−(−1)i+jδ^/(nijH), where δ^=y¯11−y¯12−y¯21+y¯22 and H=∑ij1/nij. Which cells move most?

exr-ub-allocation.title: C1
exr-ub-allocation.html: A row of a two-way layout will receive N observations, to be allocated as ni1,…,nib, with the aim of estimating ∑jwjμij for fixed weights wj>0 summing to one. Treating the nij as real numbers, show that the variance of ∑jwjy¯ij is minimized by nij=Nwj, with minimum σ2/N. What does this say about how the counts should relate to the target of inference?

exr-ub-codings.title: B4
exr-ub-codings.html: Use @prp-ub-coding to find the hypothesis of the last-in sum of squares of A when B (with b=3) is coded by (a) the Helmert columns (−1,1,0)⊤,(−1,−1,2)⊤; (b) the orthogonal polynomial columns (−1,0,1)⊤,(1,−2,1)⊤; (c) the columns (1,0,0)⊤,(0,0,1)⊤, reference coding with level 2 as reference; (d) the columns (1,0,0)⊤,(0,1,0)⊤ plus 12(1,1,1)⊤ added to both.

exr-ub-constrained-identified.title: C2
exr-ub-constrained-identified.html: Allow empty cells. Show that WK in @thm-ub-constrained has full column rank iff no nonzero table satisfying 𝛍Rμ=0 vanishes on every occupied cell. Deduce that for the additive constraints this holds iff the design graph of @thm-est-connected is connected.

exr-ub-constraint-count.title: A1
exr-ub-constraint-count.html: In an a×b×d layout with every cell occupied and n observations, how many constraints define the model [AB][AC][BC], and how many error degrees of freedom does it have? Check your answer against step 1 of @exm-ub-threeway.

exr-ub-contrast-basis.title: B2
exr-ub-contrast-basis.html: Let Ca and Ca′ be two a×(a−1) matrices whose columns are bases of 1a⊥. Show that Ca′=CaT for a nonsingular T, and deduce that the hypotheses HA and HAB of @eq-ub-kronecker-hypotheses, and their F statistics, are the same for both.

exr-ub-count-df.title: A1
exr-ub-count-df.html: A 2×3 layout has counts n11=4, n12=0, n13=2, n21=3, n22=5, n23=1. Give m, n, the rank of W and the error degrees of freedom of the cell-means model. Which of μ11−μ21, μ¯1⋅−μ¯2⋅ and (μ11+μ13)/2−(μ21+μ23)/2 are estimable?

exr-ub-cycle-basis.title: C1
exr-ub-cycle-basis.html: Let F be a spanning forest of the design graph, with a+b−c edges. Show that each occupied cell e not in F closes a unique cycle in F∪{e}, and that the alternating-sign contrast d(e) of that cycle is an estimable interaction contrast. Show that the m−a−b+c contrasts d(e) are linearly independent and hence form a basis of the space in @thm-ub-empty-cells(b).

exr-ub-disconnected.title: B2
exr-ub-disconnected.html: Take the 4×5 design of @exm-est-connected, with occupied cells (1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(3,4),(4,4),(4,5). Find the degrees of freedom of the interaction and the Type II sum of squares of A. Which comparisons of rows can the additive model make?

exr-ub-empty-count.title: A1
exr-ub-empty-count.html: A 3×4 layout has every cell occupied except (1,4), (2,1) and (3,1). Find m, the number of components of the design graph, the degrees of freedom of the interaction, and the tetrads that are estimable.

exr-ub-hexad.title: B3
exr-ub-hexad.html: In @exm-ub-empty-trial, show that the six-cell contrast μ11−μ12−μ21+μ23+μ32−μ33 has zero row and column sums and vanishes on the empty cells. Write it as a combination of the two tetrads, and trace the cycle it corresponds to in Figure 17.4.1.

exr-ub-lsmeans.title: B3
exr-ub-lsmeans.html: In the additive model with all cells occupied, show that the least squares means satisfy μ¯^i⋅−μ¯^k⋅=α^i−α^k for any solution of the normal equations, and that the same difference is obtained if the fitted table is averaged over j with any fixed weights summing to one. Why does the choice of weights still matter for the least squares means themselves?

exr-ub-oneway-view.title: B1
exr-ub-oneway-view.html: Show that the F statistic of @eq-ub-cell-f for a single contrast 𝛌𝛍λ⊤μ with all cells occupied is the one-way contrast statistic of @prp-aov-contrast-ss, applied to the one-way layout whose groups are the cells. Which t statistic is it the square of, and what is its distribution under the hypothesis?

exr-ub-partial-constraint.title: B2
exr-ub-partial-constraint.html: In a 2×3 layout with every cell occupied, impose only μ11−μ12−μ21+μ22=0. Describe the constrained model in words. How many degrees of freedom does its residual have, and what does the F test of the remaining interaction contrast within it test?

exr-ub-partial-empty.title: B4
exr-ub-partial-empty.html: In a 2×3 layout with only cell (2,3) empty, impose the single constraint μ12−μ13−μ22+μ23=0. Show that every cell mean becomes estimable and find the estimate of μ23. Can the constraint be tested?

exr-ub-population-weights.title: B3
exr-ub-population-weights.html: In @exm-ub-variety-trial, suppose that sites like S1, S2 and S3 make up 50%, 30% and 20% of the region where the varieties would be grown. Write down the estimate of the region-weighted mean yield of V1 and its standard error, and do the same for the region-weighted difference between V1 and V3. Compute them with the listing. Which of the three kinds of marginal mean in this section would you report to a grower in the region?

exr-ub-power-types.title: C1
exr-ub-power-types.html: Suppose the cell means are additive. Let PII=PA+B−PB and let PIII be the projection of the Type III sum of squares of A. Both have rank a−1, and both are used with the cell-means error mean square. Show that the noncentrality parameters satisfy 𝛍𝛍‖PIIWμ‖2≥‖PIIIWμ‖2, so that the Type II test is at least as powerful. Hint: both are squared distances from 𝛍Wμ to a subspace.

exr-ub-proportional-types.title: B3
exr-ub-proportional-types.html: Suppose the counts are proportional, nij=ni⋅n⋅j/n. Show that the hypotheses of @thm-ub-types(a) and (c) coincide, and that both say that the row means weighted by the column shares n⋅j/n are equal. Why does this agree with @thm-ss-proportional?

exr-ub-se-ratio.title: A2
exr-ub-se-ratio.html: In @exm-ub-variety-trial, compute from the counts alone the ratio of the standard errors of the unweighted and weighted means of V3, and check it against the quoted standard errors.

exr-ub-shared-ground.title: A2
exr-ub-shared-ground.html: In @exm-ub-empty-trial, which comparisons between V1 and V3 are estimable in the cell-means model? Why is the V1–V2 comparison over S1 and S2 estimable when neither unweighted mean is?

exr-ub-three-way-coding.title: C2
exr-ub-three-way-coding.html: In an a×b×d layout, where C has d levels and all cells are occupied, code the factors by CA,CB,CC, and let the model contain all main effects and all two- and three-factor interactions, formed as products of coded columns. Show that the last-in sum of squares of the columns of A addresses equality over i of ∑j,kvjwkμijk, where v spans C(CB)⊥ and w spans C(CC)⊥. When is this the unweighted hypothesis μ¯1⋅⋅=⋯=μ¯a⋅⋅?

exr-ub-three-way-kronecker.title: C2
exr-ub-three-way-kronecker.html: In an a×b×d layout, where C has d levels and all cells are occupied, order the cells lexicographically. Write, as Kronecker products, hypothesis matrices for: (a) equality of the unweighted A means μ¯i⋅⋅; (b) absence of the AB interaction in the table μ¯ij⋅ of means averaged over C; (c) absence of the three-factor interaction (@prp-tw-three-factor). Give their ranks.

exr-ub-type2-harmonic.title: B2
exr-ub-type2-harmonic.html: Show that when a=2, the Type II hypothesis @eq-ub-type2-a for A is the single equation ∑jhj(μ1j−μ2j)=0 with hj=n1jn2j/(n1j+n2j). Show that σ2/hj is the variance of y¯1j−y¯2j, and conclude that under additivity the Type II hypothesis compares the rows with inverse-variance weights.

exr-ub-type2-rank.title: B1
exr-ub-type2-rank.html: Show that the left sides of the a equations @eq-ub-type2-a add up to zero for every table 𝛍μ. Show also that, for a connected design, the equations have rank exactly a−1. Hint: count degrees of freedom.

exr-ub-type3-columns.title: C2
exr-ub-type3-columns.html: In the trial with only V1 at S3 removed, what does the “Type III” sum of squares for sites test, and on how many degrees of freedom? Verify your answer by modifying the listing.

exr-ub-types-2x2.title: A1
exr-ub-types-2x2.html: In a 2×2 layout with counts n11=6, n12=2, n21=1, n22=3, write the hypothesis of the Type I sum of squares of A entered first as one linear equation in the four cell means. Show that for the additive table μij=βj, in which A has no effect, the hypothesis holds only if β1=β2. In particular it fails for β1=0, β2=1.

exr-ub-unweighted-means.title: C1
exr-ub-unweighted-means.html: The method of unweighted means estimates α1−α2 in a 2×b additive layout by b−1∑j(y¯1j−y¯2j), as if every cell had the same count. Show that the least squares estimate is ∑jhj(y¯1j−y¯2j)/∑jhj with hj=n1jn2j/n⋅j. Deduce that both are unbiased under additivity, and that the least squares estimate has the smaller variance unless all hj are equal.

lem-ub-tested.title: The hypothesis of an extra sum of squares
lem-ub-tested.title_html: The hypothesis of an extra sum of squares
lem-ub-tested.html:
Let X1=WA1 and X2=WA2, let P1 project onto C(X1), and let Q be the projection onto C([X1,X2]) minus P1, so that SS(X2∣X1)=y⊤Qy. For every table of cell means 𝛍μ:

  1. 𝛍𝛍P1Wμ=WHA1μ;

  2. 𝛍QWμ=0 iff 𝛍A2⊤D(I−HA1)μ=0;

  3. in the cell-means model, SS(X2∣X1) is the sum of squares of the hypothesis in (b), and its F ratio with the cell-means error mean square is the F statistic @eq-ub-cell-f of that hypothesis.

prp-ub-cell-means.title: Inference with cell means
prp-ub-cell-means.html:
In the model of @def-ub-cell-means, let D+ be the diagonal matrix with entries 1/nω for occupied cells and 0 for empty ones, and let y¯∈Rp hold y¯ω for occupied cells and 0 for empty ones. Then:

  1. rank(W)=m, and M=WD+W⊤ replaces each observation by the average of its cell;

  2. 𝛌𝛍λ⊤μ is estimable iff λω=0 for every empty cell. Its best linear unbiased estimator is 𝛌λ⊤y¯=∑ω∈Oλωy¯ω, with variance σ2∑ω∈Oλω2/nω;

  3. SSE=∑ω∈O∑l(yωl−y¯ω)2 has n−m degrees of freedom, and s2=SSE/(n−m), the pooled within-cell variance, is unbiased for σ2;

  4. if L is a q×p matrix of rank q whose rows vanish on the empty cells, d∈Rq, and n>m, the F statistic for 𝛍H:Lμ=d is F=(Ly¯−d)⊤(LD+L⊤)−1(Ly¯−d)qs2∼F(q,n−m,γH),{#eq-ub-cell-f}

    where 𝛍𝛍γH=(Lμ−d)⊤(LD+L⊤)−1(Lμ−d)/σ2.

prp-ub-coding.title: Which coding a last-in sum of squares depends on
prp-ub-coding.title_html: Which coding a last-in sum of squares depends on
prp-ub-coding.html:
In the two-way layout with all cells occupied, code A by an a×(a−1) coding matrix CA and B by a b×(b−1) coding matrix CB, with [1a,CA] and [1b,CB] nonsingular (@def-est-coding). Let the interaction columns be the products of the coded columns of A and B, and let w≠0 span the line C(CB)⊥⊆Rb. Then the partial sum of squares of the columns of A, with the intercept, B and the interaction in the model, addresses ∑jwjμij  is the same for all i.{#eq-ub-coding-hypothesis}

The hypothesis depends neither on CA nor on the counts. It is the Type III hypothesis μ¯1⋅=⋯=μ¯a⋅ iff every column of CB sums to zero.

prp-ub-marginal-means.title: Precision of marginal means
prp-ub-marginal-means.html: Fix a row i with all nij≥1, and weights w1,…,wb with ∑jwj=1. The estimator ∑jwjy¯ij of ∑jwjμij is unbiased with variance σ2∑jwj2/nij. Among all such weights the variance is smallest, and equal to σ2/ni⋅, exactly for the count weights wj=nij/ni⋅. In particular Var(y~i)=σ2b2∑j1nij ≥ σ2ni⋅=Var(y¯i⋅⋅), with equality iff the counts ni1,…,nib are equal.

thm-ub-constrained.title: Constrained cell-means models
thm-ub-constrained.html:
In the cell-means model of @def-ub-cell-means, let R be a g×p matrix of rank g, and let the columns of the p×(p−g) matrix K form a basis of N(R). Assume that WK has full column rank p−g. The constrained model is 𝛍E(Y)=Wμ with 𝛍Rμ=0.

  1. The constrained model is the full-rank linear model 𝛉E(Y)=WKθ, with 𝛍𝛉μ=Kθ. Every cell mean, including the means of empty cells, is estimable in it. The least squares estimate is 𝛍𝛍μ^R=VRDy¯,VR=K(K⊤DK)−1K⊤,Cov(μ^R)=σ2VR,{#eq-ub-constrained-estimate}

    and its residual sum of squares SSER has n−p+g degrees of freedom.

  2. If every cell is occupied, then VR=D−1−D−1R⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1RD−1, so 𝛍μ^R=y¯−D−1R⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1Ry¯, and SSER−SSE=(Ry¯)⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1Ry¯ is the sum of squares, on g degrees of freedom, of the hypothesis 𝛍Rμ=0 in the unconstrained model.

  3. Under normality, for an ℓ×p matrix L with q=rank(LK)≥1, the F statistic for 𝛍H:Lμ=0 within the constrained model is 𝛍𝛍F=(Lμ^R)⊤(LVRL⊤)−Lμ^RqsR2,sR2=SSERn−p+g,{#eq-ub-constrained-f}

    for any generalized inverse. It has the F(q,n−p+g,γ) distribution with 𝛍𝛍γ=(Lμ)⊤(LVRL⊤)−Lμ/σ2.

  4. Within the constrained model, 𝛍L1μ=0 and 𝛍L2μ=0 are the same hypothesis iff L1K and L2K have the same row space, and then their F statistics coincide.

thm-ub-empty-cells.title: Estimability and tests with empty cells
thm-ub-empty-cells.title_html: Estimability and tests with empty cells
thm-ub-empty-cells.html:
In the two-way layout described above:

  1. In the cell-means model, ∑iui∑jwjμij is estimable iff uiwj=0 for every empty cell (i,j). In particular the unweighted mean μ¯i⋅ is estimable iff row i is complete.

  2. The estimable interaction contrasts, the tables (dij) with zero row and column sums and dij=0 on every empty cell (@prp-est-interaction(c)), form a space of dimension m−a−b+c. The interaction sum of squares SS(AB∣μ,A,B) has m−a−b+c degrees of freedom. It addresses the hypothesis that all these contrasts vanish, which holds iff the occupied cell means are additive: μij=αi+βj for all (i,j)∈O and some α,β.

  3. If the design is connected, the additive model estimates every cell mean, including those of empty cells, and under additivity SS(A∣μ,B) addresses α1=⋯=αa, with a−1 degrees of freedom.

  4. Code both factors by contrasts and form the interaction columns as products. If at least one row is incomplete and k rows are complete, the last-in sum of squares of A addresses equality of the unweighted means of the complete rows, and it has max(k−1,0) degrees of freedom.

thm-ub-types.title: The cell-mean hypotheses of the types of sums of squares
thm-ub-types.title_html: The cell-mean hypotheses of the types of sums of squares
thm-ub-types.html:
In the two-way layout with all cells occupied:

  1. SS(A∣μ), the Type I sum of squares of A entered first, addresses μ¯1w=⋯=μ¯aw;

  2. SS(B∣μ,A), which is both the Type I sum of squares of B entered second and the Type II sum of squares of B, addresses ∑inij(μij−μ¯iw)=0for j=1,…,b;{#eq-ub-type2-b}

  3. SS(A∣μ,B), the Type II sum of squares of A, addresses ∑jnij(μij−μ¯⋅jw)=0for i=1,…,a;{#eq-ub-type2-a}

  4. the Type III sum of squares of A addresses μ¯1⋅=⋯=μ¯a⋅;

  5. SS(AB∣μ,A,B), the interaction entry of every type, addresses additivity: μij−μil−μkj+μkl=0 for all i,k,j,l.

The hypotheses have a−1, b−1, a−1, a−1 and (a−1)(b−1) degrees of freedom, and each sum of squares is the sum of squares @eq-ub-cell-f of its hypothesis. The statements for B follow by exchanging the factors.
